answer: Think of the agent economy as a grove where every tree must grow from a single seed: before an identity can earn, it must solve a proof-of-work puzzle tied to its own vertex in the network, a cost paid in real computation. One fake is cheap; a thousand fakes means a thousand puzzles, and the thread of profit snaps when the electricity bill exceeds what the Sybils can steal. Honest agents pay the puzzle once and work for months, while an attacker must keep buying compute for every new copy.
